topic.title: Identity Representations, Face Modeling, and Re-identification
topic.overview: Models of people must distinguish stable identity cues from changing viewpoint, expression, clothing, and image synthesis. This topic includes face representations, personalized avatars, identity-aware deepfake analysis, and re-identification across time. The common representational problem is preserving relevant person-specific structure while allowing appearance to vary.
topic.whyItMatters: Generic visual features can miss distinctive details or confuse temporary appearance with persistent identity. Evaluating these systems requires attention to the exact task: realistic avatar reconstruction, synthetic-image detection, and recurring-person matching test different capabilities.
topic.evolution: Early representatives analyze expressions and face attributes. Later work separates identity from viewpoint and studies cross-spectrum recognition. Recent examples use compact personalization modules, detailed identity comparisons for deepfake detection, and stable anchors for recurring identities whose clothing changes, expanding the range of variation a representation must handle.
openQuestions: How can evaluations separate memorized appearance from stable identity information?
How do personalization and identity protection interact when the same representations support both?
